statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) through the CME weekend halt and 12 (low) in the scheduled reopen hour; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 62 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, which is the final hour of this forecast window, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in the first twenty-three hours covered here and Tail stays far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs from 25 to 45 as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the reopen and the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence eases from 62 to 56 because the reference tape is ageing rather than because the evidence has become conflicting. No danger window is published, since Tail does not reach the watch band in any slot, including the reopen hour, which is framed as a conditional checkpoint rather than an observed path.
headline: Weekend halt, hour 27: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, the 27 August H.15 2-year at 4.20% and 10-year at 4.67%, and a near coin-flip September Fed meeting after Warsh; Globex reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC inside this window
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, which falls inside this window as its final slot, so the first twenty-three hours assessed here are a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August. The pre-halt evidence set was re-verified against primary sources this run and is unchanged: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43, down 0.55 percent, within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The Federal Reserve H.15 daily release still carries 27 August as its most recent column, at 4.20 percent for the 2-year and 4.67 percent for the 10-year, because the release is not posted at weekends. The dominant driver remains Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, read as hawkish: verified current reporting describes the 16 September meeting as close to a coin flip, with futures-implied hike odds near 59 percent against roughly 35 percent beforehand, while prediction markets sit lower on Kalshi at about 48 percent and higher on Polymarket. Friday's decline was narrow rather than broad: across the tracked semiconductor set the mean change was about minus 2.5 percent, led by Arm down 6.33 percent and Nvidia down 4.57 percent, while five of eight tracked megacaps advanced, with Amazon up 3.97 percent, Alphabet up 1.74 percent and Microsoft up 1.68 percent. That breadth context is latest-session, delayed material and is used only as background, not as evidence of a live path; the shared context file was more than ninety minutes old at assessment time and was therefore treated as stale supporting context while full independent research was carried out. Energy was orderly into the weekend, with WTI at 83.44 dollars after a roughly 4 percent weekly decline, and this run's geopolitical check identified no fresh verified supply discontinuity. Verified weekend information flow has been commentary and recapitulation of the same repricing rather than new event risk, and none of it can reach a price until the venue reopens. Tail is therefore held at 5 for the twenty-three closed hours, which maps to EA_ON and green, because a closed market cannot produce the shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, repeated extension or session-extreme holding that Tail measures. The final slot, the scheduled reopen, carries a conditional Tail of 12: it allows for a weekend gap and thin Sunday-evening liquidity while remaining well below the block threshold, since a single thin hour rarely sustains the no-retracement path Tail is defined against, and no post-reopen alignment is counted as observed before a path prints. Stress rises from 25 to 45 across the window as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows into the reopen and into the 1 to 4 September data stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, Broadcom results, ISM Services and the August payrolls report. Confidence eases from 62 to 56 as the Friday reference tape ages past two days; the decline is a freshness adjustment, since the evidence set is complete and primary-source verified rather than conflicting.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from the late Friday post-close futures hour through hour 26 of the weekend halt. The mode was normal in every slot and the mapped policy state never left EA_ON. Tail decayed from 6 to 5 within the first three hours and then held the 5 floor for the remaining twenty-one, because no venue was open to produce the price-path evidence Tail is defined against. Stress fell to a 22 trough in the early hours of Saturday and then held a 25 plateau for the last eighteen hours, while Confidence declined steadily from 84 to 63 as the Friday reference tape aged without any new observable structure. No hour in the window carried a danger window and no hour was unavailable.
outlookSummary: The first twenty-three hours of this window fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; Tail is held at 5 throughout, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON, and the dominant mode is normal in those slots because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. The final slot is the scheduled Globex reopen at Sunday 22:00 UTC, the first hour in this window that can host observable structure: it is published with a conditional Tail of 12 and a mixed mode, which allows for a weekend gap and thin Sunday-evening liquidity while staying below the watch band, because hypothetical post-reopen alignment is not treated as observed before a path prints. Stress ramps from 25 to 45, crossing into the elevated band in the last three slots as the stock of unpriced weekend information meets the reopen and the 1 to 4 September data stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, Broadcom results, ISM Services and the August payrolls report, with the 16 September FOMC decision priced close to a coin flip behind it. Confidence eases from 62 to 56 as the Friday reference tape ages past two days. No danger window is published, and the size and direction of any reopen gap is a checkpoint for a later assessment rather than a published risk here.
